# requires: transfer
#
# The file is the floor. A checkpoint claiming forty proven bytes over a partial
# that holds twenty: the claim is cut down to what is on disk, the hash is
# rebuilt over the kept prefix, and the transfer carries on from twenty. The
# partial is never deleted, because deleting a prefix that is about to be
# verified anyway is the 40 GB this layer exists not to fetch twice.
#
# Go and C++ deleted the file and refused until 2026-09-06, Python did what
# download/README.md's first guarantee says, and the two texts contradicted each
# other in writing for as long as both existed. Every other scenario was green
# throughout: a harness that compares implementations to each other can see a
# disagreement about this rule and cannot see the rule.
submit A size=64 digest=good src=file
claim A alpha 5000
stage A 20
progress A alpha 40 {"verified_prefix":40}
release A alpha
run A beta
orphans
state A

# expect 6: ok state=transferred [DL-R3]
# expect 6: done=64 err=none [DL-R4]
# expect 7: ok -
